defs_parts: Six labels sit in the corners of the pictures that follow.
In the book text: the course text uses and explains the term.
In the glossary: the term is on the course term list, but the text does not explain it.
Outside source: the term comes from a source outside the course text.
Computed: the numbers are worked out on screen from stated inputs.
Simulation: a model run step by step from stated rules, not a measurement of a real game.
Conceptual: a drawing of the idea, with no data behind it.
recap_lines: An agent senses, decides and acts, once on every tick.
Sight range is a distance only, and line of sight needs a clear line.
Seek never slows, and arrive slows down to stop on the target.
Separation, alignment and cohesion together make a flock emerge.
Dijkstra expands by cost so far, and A star adds an estimate toward the goal.
An admissible heuristic never overestimates, so A star finds the cheapest path.
bookends.command: Quiz me on game AI terms with short game-making cases, one at a time. Use the terms sight range, line of sight, field-of-view cone, seek, arrive, pursue, separation, cohesion, Dijkstra and A star. For each case I must name the exact term and say why its look-alike is wrong. Hold back the answer until I reply, then tell me if I was right.
checks: Check: each case is a game situation, and the answer waits for your reply.
Check: you named the exact term and said why its look-alike does not fit.
